trigger: a crash or concurrent generator run during write_bytes leaves a truncated file
classification_rationale: write is non-atomic before and after; the next run's compare detects a truncated file and rewrites (measured by up/m4); unchanged-path reduces exposure (measured: 0 torn reads vs 9464 on old in steady state)

trigger: the existing output file cannot be read (permissions, path is a directory) so it is rewritten without proof the bytes differ
classification_rationale: docstring says 'rewritten only when its bytes differ'; on the OSError-on-read path it is rewritten without a compare. consistency-auditor judged this an acceptable conservative simplification (extra write, never a skipped one); build-ci owns the truth call
summary: Optional wording: 'rewritten only when its bytes are unchanged on disk' is not true either; 'is not rewritten when its bytes already match' is exact. Operator choice.

trigger: build dir restored/rsynced (or clock stepped back) so bundled_content.cpp mtime is in the future relative to its .o
classification_rationale: new persistent state: an 'unchanged' run keeps the future mtime, so ninja recompiles+relinks every run until wall-clock passes it (old code reset the mtime to now each run but relinked every run anyway: equal per-run cost). Self-limiting; recovery is touch or any content change. Not pager-grade (sre).
summary: Measured in a scratch project: old 3 link steps per run, new 3 per run until the clock catches up (+3 s case: 3,3,3,0). Optional: a code comment. No action recommended.

summary: unhappy-path labelled it speculative; a code path and trigger are named, so recorded likely per the preamble definition. No action.
